title: ATS-Friendly CV Section Headings for Nigerian Job Seekers
excerpt: Master ATS-friendly section headings to get your CV past Nigerian employers' screening systems. Essential tips for job seekers.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: Your CV's section headings might seem like a minor detail, but they're crucial for getting past Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) used by Nigerian employers. From banks like Access Bank to tech companies like Flutterwave, most organizations now rely on ATS software to filter resumes before human recruiters ever see them.

Using the wrong section headings can cause your CV to be automatically rejected, no matter how qualified you are. This comprehensive guide will show you exactly how to write ATS-friendly section headings that Nigerian employers' systems can easily read and categorize.
Why ATS-Friendly Section Headings Matter in Nigeria

Applicant Tracking Systems scan your CV for specific keywords and formatting patterns. When you use unconventional or creative section headings, the ATS might not recognize important information about your background. This is particularly important in Nigeria's competitive job market, where companies like MTN, Dangote Group, and PwC Nigeria receive hundreds of applications for each position.

The ATS needs to quickly identify and categorize your information into standard fields like work experience, education, and skills. If your section headings don't match what the system expects, your CV could be marked as incomplete or difficult to parse, automatically lowering your ranking.

Nigerian companies increasingly use international ATS platforms like Workday, BambooHR, and Greenhouse. These systems are programmed to recognize standard English section headings, making it essential to use conventional terminology.

Make sure all your section headings follow the same format:

items: Same font style (bold or bold with underlining)
Consistent capitalization (Title Case or ALL CAPS)
Proper spacing above and below headings
Text boxes or tables for headings
Images or logos as section dividers

body.text: Stick to standard fonts like Arial, Calibri, or Times New Roman for maximum ATS compatibility across Nigerian employers' systems.

items: Use colons sparingly: "Skills:" is acceptable but "Skills" is better
Avoid exclamation marks or question marks
Don't use quotation marks around headings
Skip periods at the end of headings

body.text: Common Mistakes Nigerian Job Seekers Make
Avoid these creative alternatives that can confuse ATS systems:

items: "What I Bring to the Table" instead of "Skills"

body.text: While Nigeria is multilingual, ATS systems work best with:

items: No mixing of English with local languages
Use either "Work Experience" or "Employment History" throughout
Stick with "Education" rather than mixing with "Academic Background"
